content: Atom 0 is the pyridine 4-methyl on this host, acyclic bond to atom 1, so the usual anchor. The geometry of the central ring turned out to be the most valuable variable in this whole series - para gives 0.41, meta gives 0.50 - and I have never tested the third possibility. An ortho arrangement puts the two nitrogens on adjacent carbons, which is a genuinely different shape: it brings the anilide carbonyl close enough to the arylamine N-H to hydrogen bond intramolecularly and forces the two rings nearly coplanar. That could either lock the molecule into the conformation the model likes, or quench the donor I know is essential. Either answer is worth having, and it completes the scan so I never have to guess at this again. I keep everything else at its best measured setting: 4-methyl on the pyridine, cyclopropanecarboxamide cap, plain benzene centre, both N-H donors free. Expected product: N-{2-[(4-methylpyridin-2-yl)amino]phenyl}cyclopropanecarboxamide at about 267 Da.
